questions.stem: All of the following statements are true regarding spider telangiectasias except:

options.label: B
options.text: These manifest as radial, often pulsatile arrays of dilated subcutaneous arteries or arterioles about a central core

options.label: C
options.text: These commonly occur on the face, neck, or upper chest

options.label: D
options.text: These are most frequently associated with hyperestrogenic states, such as pregnancy or liver cirrhosis

questions.solutionHtml:
These are neoplastic lesions

Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 519

questions.stem: All of the following statements are true regarding hemangioma except:

options.label: A
options.text: These are present from birth and initially increase in size, but many eventually regress

options.label: B
options.text: Hemangioma typically are localized lesions confined to the head and neck

options.label: C
options.text: Nearly one-third of these internal lesions are found in the lung

questions.answerText: Nearly one-third of these internal lesions are found in the lung
questions.solutionHtml:
Nearly one-third of these internal lesions are found in the lung
  • False, nearly one-third of internal lesions occur in the liver.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 519, 520

questions.stemHtml: The histopathological picture of blood-filled vascular channels separated by connective tissue stroma identifies the lesion:
questions.solutionHtml:
Cavernous hemangioma
  • On histologic examination, the mass is unencapsulated, has infiltrative borders, and is composed of large, cavernous blood-filled vascular spaces separated by connective tissue stroma, suggestive of Cavernous Hemangioma.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 519, 520

questions.stem: A pregnancy tumor is a type of-
questions.solutionHtml:
Pyogenic hemangioma
  • Pregnancy tumor (granuloma gravidarum) is a pyogenic granuloma that occurs infrequently (1% of patients) in the gingiva of pregnant women.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 519, 520

questions.stemHtml: A patient has repeated trauma over the gingival mucosa and presented to the clinician as a red pedunculated lesion that bleeds on the touch and is ulcerated, surgical excision was done, and histopathological picture shows. Identify the lesion:
questions.solutionHtml:
Pyogenic granuloma

Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 519, 520

questions.stem: Which of the following is classified into the intermediate grade neoplasm in the classification of vascular tumors and tumor-like conditions:
questions.solutionHtml:
Hemangioendothelioma
  • Malignant neoplasm
    • Angiosarcoma
    • Hemangiopericytoma
  • Intermediate grade neoplasm
    • Kaposi sarcoma
    • Hemangioendothelioma


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 520- 522

questions.stem: All of the following statements are true regarding malignant vascular tumors except:

options.label: A
options.text: They are more cellular and proliferative

options.label: D
options.text: Usually confirmed by CD 31 or von Willebrand factor

questions.solutionHtml:
They form obvious vascular channels
  • Malignant vascular tumors are more cellular and more proliferative, and exhibit cytologic atypia; they usually do NOT form well-organized vessels.
  • The endothelial origin of these tumors can be demonstrated by immunohistochemical staining for CD31 or von Willebrand factor.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 522, 523
